summary: Douglas County, OR lookout site: 16-ft tree-then-tower lookout on Silica Mountain, tower built 1931, removed or destroyed about 1965; registered as a former site in 2011.

facts.design: 16-ft round fir tower with twelve legs and a 14 x 14 ft gable-roof cab; described by FFLOS as a 16 ft wooden live-in tower
facts.status_note: Removed about 1965 per FFLOS; firelookout.com says destroyed about 1965. Registered as a former site in 2011.
facts.agency: Douglas FPA (Douglas County Fire Patrol); site first on Umpqua National Forest

events.note: Lookout established in a tree 30 ft above the ground (Oregon Lookouts timeline)

September 1927 Eugene Guard: emergency lookout stationed at Silica mountain; Sentinel report describes a fir cut off at 60 ft with a fire-finding perch and a ladder up the side; no lookout went up top except by special order or when a lightning storm was expected or under way
16-ft round fir tower with twelve legs and a 14 x 14 gable-roof cab (Oregon Lookouts); FFLOS and firelookout.com both give 1931
CCC crew from the Brice Creek camp sent to Silica to maintain trails and telephone lines (The Sentinel, July 21, 1933)
Removed about 1965 (FFLOS); firelookout.com says destroyed about 1965
Registered March 29, 2011 as FFLOS US 904, OR 271; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the tower was removed about 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed about 1965. The date agrees; the verb differs. The story reports both.
The 1920 timeline entry gives a lookout in a tree 30 ft up; the 1927 newspaper gives a fir cut to 60 ft with a perch. The sources do not say they are the same tree.

The Oregon Lookouts page says the site was first on the Umpqua National Forest and later run by the Douglas County Fire Patrol; FFLOS lists Douglas FPA as administrator. These describe different periods and do not conflict.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes what, if anything, remains at the site today, and no access information was found. A search returned only register and list pages. The 1931 build year agrees across all three sources. The removal year is approximate (about 1965) and the verb differs between sources. firelookout.com credits a photo to Mark Swift, and the Oregon Lookouts page mentions a 1933 panorama; neither has an image URL in the cached pages, so no photos were added.
